e05a2ab3577e9f7c: From Moaz Nair
In any healthy democracy, a vibrant opposition is not a luxury; it is a necessity.
Its role extends far beyond merely opposing the government of the day. It must act as a credible government-in-waiting, offering a distinct, actionable alternative vision for the nation’s progress.
Unfortunately, in contemporary Malaysian politics, the federal opposition — represented by Perikatan Nasional (PN) — is falling drastically short of this democratic mandate.
In the eyes of ordinary citizens, they are increasingly failing to project the image of a responsible, cohesive team capable of governing.
Instead of elevating national discourse, recent parliamentary sessions have frequently devolved into political circuses.
Rather than acting as serious lawmakers, some opposition figures have behaved more like clowns, relying on histrionics, disruptions, and shouting matches to capture headlines.
Consider the chaotic session during the 2026 Supply Bill debate, which descended into an embarrassing shouting match.

The Dewan Rakyat witnessed the unseemly spectacle of opposition members trading insults like “gila” (crazy) and “mabuk” (drunk) with a government backbencher over religious rhetoric concerning alcohol, ultimately leading to an opposition MP being ejected from the august House.
Deficit of substance

The opposition’s core problem lies in a severe deficit of substance. A constructive opposition should serve as a vital check on power by scrutinising legislation, advocating for fiscal discipline, and consistently raising structured concerns regarding governance, transparency, and inflation.

While PN is quick to criticise the current administration’s landmark policy decisions — such as the highly contentious targeted rationalisation of fuel and electricity subsidies and the introduction of digital and carbon taxes — their criticisms often exist in a vacuum.
When civil society and economic think tanks called on PN to present a costed alternative framework to address middle-class cost-of-living pressures, the response was telling.

The opposition leadership flatly dismissed the necessity of drawing up an alternative national budget, calling the exercise “syok sendiri” (self-indulgent) because it would have no chance of being implemented by the current government.
This defeatist stance reveals a fatal misunderstanding of the opposition’s purpose. It is easy to point out a leak in the roof; it is much harder to present the architectural blueprint to fix it.
This lack of policy depth is directly tied to the underutilisation and internal instability of PN’s own structures.

Although the coalition established portfolio committees to function as a shadow cabinet, key leaders have come under heavy fire for failing to drive substantive policy debates or introduce impactful private members’ bills.
The opposition has been sharply criticised for failing to produce a counter-economic blueprint, focusing instead on reactive politics.

Meanwhile, the opposition’s structural credibility took an unprecedented hit when the Registrar of Societies (RoS) cancelled Perikatan Nasional’s registration following fierce infighting between PAS and Bersatu, with top figures in Bersatu publicly blasting the coalition leadership for failing to manage the bloc with democratic principles and transparency.
Over-reliance on identity politics

Compounding this policy vacuum is PN’s over-reliance on identity politics. Analysts have repeatedly noted that the opposition disproportionately prioritises divisive racial and religious rhetoric over concrete economic solutions.
While proponents argue that this positions PN as the champion of a conservative, nationalist vision for Malaysia, this narrow focus inherently alienates the nation’s diverse, multi-ethnic electorate.
A vision built purely on identity cannot resolve currency fluctuations, fix the healthcare system, or improve the quality of education.

Malaysia faces complex global and domestic headwinds that demand rigorous intellectual debate. By choosing rhetorical fireworks over structural alternatives, the federal opposition is letting down the very citizens it aims to represent.

To become a credible alternative government, PN must move past the circus acts, put its shadow cabinet to work, resolve its internal chaos, and prove to Malaysians that they can govern with intellect rather than identity and empty rhetoric.
Moaz Nair is an FMT reader.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
9d8a3e0ef2f7c3e3: Dalam mana-mana sistem demokrasi yang sihat, pembangkang yang dinamik bukanlah satu kemewahan, sebaliknya ia merupakan satu keperluan. Peranannya menjangkau jauh daripada sekadar menentang kerajaan sedia ada. Ia mesti bertindak sebagai sebuah 'kerajaan dalam penantian' (government-in-waiting) yang berwibawa, dengan menawarkan visi alternatif yang jelas dan boleh dilaksana demi kemajuan negara.

Malangnya, dalam landskap politik kontemporari, pembangkang persekutuan -- yang diwakili oleh koalisi Perikatan Nasional (PN) -- dilihat gagal memenuhi mandat demokratik ini. Di mata rakyat biasa, mereka semakin gagal menampilkan diri sebagai sebuah pasukan yang bertanggungjawab, bersatu padu, dan mampu mentadbir negara.

Sidang Parlimen kebelakangan ini sebaliknya sering kali bertukar menjadi seperti sarkas politik, bukannya mempertingkat kualiti wacana nasional. Daripada bertindak sebagai penggubal undang-undang yang berwibawa, segelintir tokoh pembangkang lebih gemar berkelakuan seperti badut, dengan bergantung kepada gimik, gangguan, dan pertengkaran mulut semata-mata untuk meraih perhatian media.

Soroti sahaja sidang yang kecoh semasa perbahasan RUU Bekalan 2026, yang melarat menjadi pertengkaran mulut yang memalukan. Dewan Rakyat menyaksikan gelagat sumbang ahli pembangkang saling bertukar hinaan melampau seperti 'gila' dan 'mabuk' dengan penyokong kerajaan berhubung retorik agama berkaitan alkohol, yang akhirnya menyebabkan seorang Ahli Parlimen pembangkang diarah keluar dari Dewan yang mulia itu.

Masalah utama pihak pembangkang berakar umbi daripada defisit isi yang kritikal. Pembangkang yang konstruktif sepatutnya berfungsi sebagai rujukan semak dan imbang yang penting terhadap kuasa eksekutif dengan meneliti undang-undang, menyuarakan disiplin fiskal, serta konsisten membangkitkan kebimbangan yang berstruktur mengenai tadbir urus, ketelusan, dan inflasi.

Walaupun PN pantas mengkritik keputusan dasar utama pentadbiran semasa -- seperti pelaksanaan rasionalisasi subsidi bahan api dan elektrik yang mencetuskan kontroversi serta pengenalan cukai digital dan karbon -- kritikan mereka sebenarnya retorik kosong tanpa alternatif.

Apabila masyarakat sivil dan badan pemikir ekonomi menggesa PN mengemukakan rangka kerja alternatif berserta kos yang jelas bagi menangani tekanan kos sara hidup golongan kelas pertengahan, respons yang diberikan amat mengecewakan. Kepimpinan pembangkang secara bulat-bulat menolak keperluan merangka belanjawan negara alternatif, malah menyifatkan usaha tersebut sebagai 'syok sendiri' kerana mendakwa ia tidak akan berpeluang untuk dilaksanakan oleh kerajaan sedia ada.

Sikap ini mendedahkan salah faham yang besar terhadap fungsi sebenar pembangkang. Memang mudah untuk menuding jari kepada bumbung yang bocor; namun menyedia dan membentangkan pelan seni bina untuk membaikinya adalah satu tugas yang jauh lebih mencabar.

Kekurangan dasar yang mendalam ini berkait rapat dengan kegagalan mengoptimumkan fungsi serta ketidakstabilan dalaman struktur PN sendiri. Walaupun koalisi berkenaan menubuhkan jawatankuasa portfolio untuk bertindak sebagai Kabinet bayangan, pemimpin-pemimpin utamanya dibidas kerana gagal memacu perdebatan dasar secara mendalam mahupun mengemukakan rang undang-undang (RUU) persendirian yang memberi impak.
Pihak pembangkang dikritik kerana gagal menghasilkan rangka tindakan ekonomi tandingan, sebaliknya lebih selesa menumpukan perhatian kepada politik reaktif.

Pada masa yang sama, kredibiliti struktur pembangkang menerima tamparan hebat apabila Jabatan Pendaftaran Pertubuhan Malaysia membatalkan pendaftaran PN ekoran perbalahan dalaman yang sengit antara PAS dan Bersatu, dengan tokoh-tokoh utama Bersatu secara terbuka mengecam kepimpinan koalisi kerana gagal menguruskan blok tersebut berdasarkan prinsip demokrasi dan ketelusan.

Memburukkan lagi vakum dasar ini adalah pergantungan keterlaluan kepada politik identiti. Para penganalisis sering melihat bahawa pihak pembangkang memberi keutamaan kepada retorik perkauman dan keagamaan yang memecahbelahkan berbanding penyelesaian ekonomi yang konkrit.

Walaupun penyokong berhujah bahawa pendekatan ini meletakkan PN sebagai pejuang visi nasionalis-konservatif, fokus yang sempit ini secara tidak langsung menjauhkan sokongan daripada kumpulan pengundi pelbagai kaum dan etnik. Visi yang dibina semata-mata atas paksi identiti tidak akan mampu menyelesaikan isu turun naik mata wang, memulihkan sistem penjagaan kesihatan, mahupun memperbaik kualiti pendidikan.

Malaysia kini sedang berdepan dengan cabaran global dan domestik yang rumit, yang menuntut perbahasan intelektual yang matang serta teliti. Dengan memilih gimik retorik berbanding alternatif struktur yang membina, pembangkang persekutuan sebenarnya sedang mengecewakan rakyat yang kononnya diwakili oleh mereka.

Untuk diiktiraf sebagai sebuah alternatif kerajaan yang berwibawa, PN mesti meninggalkan aksi sarkas politik, mengaktifkan Kabinet bayangan dengan berkesan, menyelesaikan kemelut dalaman, dan membuktikan kepada rakyat bahawa mereka mampu mentadbir dengan bersandarkan kebijaksanaan intelek, bukannya politik identiti dan retorik kosong.
Artikel ini adalah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.
5c12eb81d7d06edb: PETALING JAYA: A bowl of mi kolok, a slice of kek lapis and a plate of uthappam may not look as though they belong in the same conversation as historic parliamentary maces or centuries-old manuscripts.
Yet all feature in Malaysia’s latest national heritage announcement, part of a 69-item list spanning food, traditions, objects and living cultural practitioners.

Also recognised are the Gawai Dayak and Tadau Kaamatan festivals, as well as Baba Nyonya wedding customs. They join Malaysian breakfast culture and traditional foods such as nasi kandar, kacang pool, apam Johol, kuih chang, char koay kak and pasembur.

The range extends further still, taking in the sompoton (Sabah mouth organ), traditional clogs, copper craft, heirloom jars, woven textiles, and legends such as those of Mahsuri and Puteri Santubong, as well as historic objects including the Dewan Rakyat and Dewan Negara maces.

There is, however, an important distinction within the announcement. Of the 69 items recognised under National Heritage 2026, 39 had been formally declared at the time, while a further 30 were still due to be gazetted.

Under the National Heritage Act 2005, the minister may declare a heritage site, heritage object, underwater cultural heritage or living person as national heritage through an order published in the gazette.

The Act sets out a range of factors that may be considered, including historical importance, design or aesthetic qualities, scientific or technical achievement, social or cultural associations, educational value, rarity, and whether something represents a particular type of heritage.

National heritage is also distinct from Unesco recognition. The United Nations agency maintains separate international lists for cultural and natural heritage, as well as for intangible cultural heritage, which can include traditions, performing arts, rituals, festive events and traditional craftsmanship.

The framework for national heritage is, therefore, broad enough to encompass practices, traditions, objects and people whose significance lies in what they represent within Malaysian history and culture.

Deputy tourism, arts and culture minister Chiew Choon Man said the process involves screening, research and technical assessment by the heritage commissioner, while the final authority to make a declaration rests with the minister.
He also described the status as more than ceremonial recognition, saying national heritage items receive legal protection and are prioritised in preservation and conservation efforts.

This year’s list also recognises 11 living cultural practitioners, including Che Nasir Yusoff for Kelantan shadow puppetry, Salbiah Muhi for keringkam embroidery, and Siow Ho Phiew for lion dance performance and lion-head craftsmanship.
f8cf5d62704f7815: KUALA LUMPUR: Perdana Menteri, Anwar Ibrahim menduduki tempat ke-13 dalam edisi 2027 "The Muslim 500: The World's 500 Most Influential Muslims" yang diterbitkan Royal Islamic Strategic Studies Centre berpangkalan di Jordan.

Menurut edisi tahunan ke-18 penerbitan itu yang boleh diakses menerusi https://themuslim500.com, Anwar mula memegang jawatan perdana menteri Malaysia ke-10 pada November 2022, menerajui kerajaan perpaduan di bawah gabungan Pakatan Harapan (PH).

Laporan itu menyatakan Anwar yang juga menteri kewangan mengutamakan strategi peralihan digital dan ekonomi mantap menerusi kerangka Malaysia Madani yang menjadi gagasan beliau, dengan meletakkan kecerdasan buatan, semikonduktor, pusat data, pengkomputeran awan serta peralihan tenaga sebagai teras agenda strategik kerajaan.

"Pada Jun 2026, Anwar mengetengahkan peralihan tenaga sebagai tonggak utama agenda pembangunan Malaysia, dengan menghubungkan keperluan tenaga masa depan negara secara langsung kepada perkembangan pesat sektor infrastruktur berteknologi tinggi," menurut laporan itu.

Di peringkat serantau, penerbitan itu turut menonjolkan peranan Anwar sebagai orang tengah dalam isu keamanan konstruktif di Asia Tenggara, khususnya menerusi inisiatif diplomatik bagi meredakan ketegangan dan membina kepercayaan antara Thailand dengan Kemboja susulan pertempuran di sempadan pada Julai 2025.

"Selaku perdana menteri Malaysia dan pengerusi Asean, beliau menjadi tuan rumah bagi rundingan antara pemimpin kedua-dua negara di Putrajaya yang membantu mencapai persetujuan gencatan senjata. Anwar membantu membina kepercayaan antara Bangkok dengan Phnom Penh, sekali gus memperkukuh imej Malaysia sebagai perantara keamanan konstruktif di Asia Tenggara."

The Muslim 500 mengiktiraf Anwar antara ketua negara paling lantang di dunia dalam memperjuangkan isu Palestin, dengan mengekalkan sokongan teguh negara terhadap perlindungan orang awam dan akses kepada bantuan kemanusiaan di Gaza.

"Dengan mengambil pendirian tegas di pentas antarabangsa, Anwar mengumumkan kepada Parlimen bahawa negara sedang menerajui gabungan teras antarabangsa yang merangka resolusi rasmi untuk mengusir Israel daripada Pertubuhan Bangsa-bangsa Bersatu (PBB). Anwar mengulangi pendirian Malaysia sama sekali tidak mengiktiraf Israel adalah kekal."

Laporan itu menyatakan pertemuan Anwar dengan pegawai Hamas, termasuk pemimpinnya dan Allahyarham Ismail Haniyeh, mencetuskan bantahan terbuka daripada negara Barat, namun ditolak secara jelas oleh perdana menteri sambil menegaskan hak mutlak Malaysia sebagai negara berdaulat untuk menentukan dasar luarnya sendiri.

Selain kepimpinan politik, pengiktirafan itu turut merakamkan penglibatan awal Anwar dalam aktivisme sebagai pengasas dan presiden Angkatan Belia Islam Malaysia pada 1971, selain pengalamannya menerajui beberapa portfolio Kabinet, termasuk timbalan perdana menteri dan menteri kewangan pada 1990-an.

Laporan itu turut mengetengahkan sumbangan besarnya dalam bidang akademik, dengan memegang jawatan sebagai ahli akademik pelawat di St Antony’s College, Oxford, Johns Hopkins University, dan Universiti Georgetown.

"Beliau ialah pengasas bersama International Institute of Islamic Thought yang ditubuhkan di Amerika Syarikat pada 1981. Selain itu, beliau juga pernah berkhidmat sebagai Pro-Canselor di Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Malaysia dari 1983 hingga 1988 serta menerima pelbagai ijazah kehormat antarabangsa."

Dalam edisi 2027, kedudukan teratas dikongsi Raja Arab Saudi, Raja Salman bin Abdul-Aziz Al-Saud dan Putera Mahkota Mohammed bin Salman, Perdana Menteri Pakistan Mian Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif dan Ketua Staf Tentera Darat Syed Asim Munir serta Presiden Turki Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

Pemimpin Asia Tenggara lain yang turut tersenarai dalam kelompok 50 teratas termasuklah Presiden Indonesia Prabowo Subianto pada kedudukan ke-16, Pengerusi Nahdlatul Ulama Yahya Cholil Staquf (ke-21) dan ulama Indonesia Habib Luthfi bin Yahya (ke-31).

Pakar pediatrik Palestin dan Pengarah Hospital Kamal Adwan, Dr Hussam Abu Safiya, yang ditahan Israel tanpa pertuduhan sejak Disember 2024 dinobatkan "The Muslim 500's Man of the Year for 2027" dan menduduki tempat ke-50 dalam senarai itu.
40fa86114de5e32b: WASHINGTON: Pete Hegseth on Thursday awarded a medal to a US soldier who reprimanded the defense chief and his entourage for laughing and talking near the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier the day before.

Hegseth "proudly awarded Specialist Thomas Iglesias the Joint Service Commendation Medal for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on November 11, 2026," a Pentagon official said.
A post on Hegseth's official X account included photos showing him pinning the medal on the soldier's uniform and shaking his hand.
"We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist," text accompanying the photos said.

The tomb, at Arlington National Cemetery near Washington, is a sacred burial place of American military personnel killed during World War I, World War II and the Korean War. It also includes an empty site for a Vietnam War soldier in honor of missing troops from that conflict.
Video on US networks and social media showed Hegseth and his entourage gathering to take photos Wednesday at the tomb after a Veterans Day ceremony.
"All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times!" a US Army sentinel yelled loudly in response to audible laughter and chatter.

CNN identified the group taking photos on the steps near the tomb with Hegseth as his wife Jennifer, chief of staff Ricky Buria, deputy chief of staff Patrick Weaver and senior advisor Tami Radabaugh.
The tomb is patrolled at all times by soldiers who volunteer for the job and undergo "a strict selection process and intensive training," according to cemetery's website.
8d3ff53985a014a4: MELAKA, Nov 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants to hold further discussions with Anthony Loke over the Seremban MP’s resignation as Transport Minister.
Anwar said he had yet to make a decision on Loke’s resignation letter, which he had received earlier, as he wanted to discuss the matter with him first.
“Yes, Loke did write to me tendering his immediate resignation, but as Prime Minister, I have not accepted it.
“For now, he wants to take a short break, and that is fine. But we need to discuss his resignation again,” he said at the Grand Finale of the Melaka PH Rumah Kita tour in Bukit Baru here today.
Anwar said Loke had a clean and trustworthy track record in government and had worked hard to introduce various initiatives at the Transport Ministry for the benefit of the people.
“We appointed Loke as a minister because he is trustworthy and clean. He works hard and has put forward many proposals, projects and programmes to make travel easier for the public and taxi drivers.

“He is among the hardest-working ministers and is well regarded by ministry officials. That is why I said it is strange that people want a good minister like him to step down, while asking those who perform poorly to stay on. What kind of upside-down world is this?” he said.

On Tuesday, Loke announced that he was resigning with immediate effect following the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
The court ordered that Najib, 73, serve the remainder of his sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest at his residence in Langgak Duta, with immediate effect.
Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin made the ruling after setting aside an order issued by the Kuala Lumpur High Court Criminal Registry on Nov 6.

Under the new order, Najib will remain under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, before returning to Kajang Prison on Aug 24, 2028, to serve his sentence in the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) case. — Bernama

4ee7dd80f05a40dd: MELAKA, Nov 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has denied allegations that he or the government had acted against the wishes of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia over the issue of implementing house arrest for former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak.
The Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman said his administration had always upheld the constitutional monarchy system and adhered to established legal processes.

Anwar said the decision to place him under house arrest did not fall within his authority as Prime Minister, while the Attorney-General’s decision to bring the matter to court aligned with his responsibility to uphold the rule of law.
“They accused me of being disloyal to the King. I am the Prime Minister, and the King called me this afternoon. We have a good relationship.

“…Datuk Seri Najib has been in prison for four years; to allow him to serve his sentence under house arrest is not within my authority. My authority is governed by the law,” he said at the “Ngopi Santai” programme held in conjunction with the 16th Melaka state election in Ayer Molek here yesterday.

The Kuala Lumpur High Court on Tuesday ordered Najib to serve the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International case under house arrest at his residence in Langgak Duta here, with immediate effect.
Meanwhile, Anwar said sound governance, free from leakages and corruption, had enabled the government to channel various forms of assistance directly to the people.

He said this included an allocation of RM16 billion for the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) programmes, RM18 billion for this year’s public service salary adjustment, as well as RM200 in schooling assistance next year.

At the programme, Anwar also urged voters in the Ayer Molek state constituency to give PH candidate Muhammad Hakimin a chance to serve as their elected representative in Saturday’s 16th Melaka state election. — Bernama

fe43732b6c8324ac: NAIROBI: Around 520 Ethiopians sentenced to death for drug trafficking are currently awaiting execution in Saudi Arabia, the government of Tigray, a region in northern Ethiopia, said Thursday.
Most of those facing execution come from the Tigray region, said Hayish Sibagadis, head of the Youth Affairs Bureau of the Tigray regional government, at a press conference.
Riyadh announced on Wednesday that it had executed two Ethiopians for drug trafficking, a week after executing five others for the same crime.
This followed five Ethiopians executed in June and another five in July.
In total, 34 Ethiopians have been executed in Saudi Arabia in 2026, according to an AFP tally based on official statements.
"Those sentenced to death were either deceived by brokers and drawn into drug trafficking or were simply accompanying people who were carrying drugs", he said.
"Most were tried without a lawyer, in a language they did not understand, and without an interpreter," he added.
Ethiopia, which maintains good relations with Saudi Arabia, should ask Riyadh to "show mercy and spare their lives", he said.
The Ethiopian federal government did not respond to a request for comment from AFP.
Thousands of Ethiopians work in low-skilled jobs in Saudi Arabia. Most of them take the perilous "Eastern Route" from the Horn of Africa to the oil-rich kingdom via Yemen.
Tigray is a region in northern Ethiopia ravaged by a war between 2020 and 2022 that claimed at least 600,000 lives, according to African Union estimates.

168f3479ff5c6360: PETALING JAYA: An Astro cameraman dismissed for allegedly streaming Astro Ceria content illegally via his personal account has been awarded RM474,240 by the Kuala Lumpur Industrial Court which ruled his sacking was unjust.

Industrial Court chairman Augustine Anthony said the domestic inquiry (DI) panel, which found Chen Ken Tatt guilty, had improperly shifted the burden of proof onto the employee to show he was not the person who streamed AstroGo content into the illegal app HotTV.
He said that having made the accusation, Astro Facilities Sdn Bhd bore the responsibility to prove it. The award was handed down on Oct 27.

Anthony said the panel had relied heavily on the testimony of the company’s witness, its former head of intellectual property protection unit Brendan Lopez Michael, and placed the claimant in an “unenviable and helpless state” by shifting the burden of proof onto him to show he was not the culprit.

He also noted that the witness contradicted himself by speculating on various ways the illegal streaming could have occurred — including a suggestion that Chen’s wife or son might have done it if Chen had shared his mobile one-time password (OTP) with them.

“Unfortunately for the company, this sequence of evidence, which dabbled into the realm of conjecture, not only unfairly accused the claimant and his family but was devoid of any cogent evidence to prove the trail of actions or activities by the claimant, his wife or son.

“In order to prove that it was the claimant who had intentionally committed the illegal act of streaming the programme or content or negligently caused the same, more is needed than merely showing that the claimant’s AstroGo account was used for that purpose,” he said.
Anthony also said the company’s evidence of dark web searches showing Chen’s login details had not been leaked — used to infer no third party was involved — was inconclusive proof of guilt.
He added that the company’s witnesses could not explain how the dark web searches were conducted.

“Apart from the above shoddy conclusion and unsupported inferences drawn by the company, it also did not go any further to check or conduct forensic investigation on all the claimant’s or his family's devices to establish any link between the illegal streaming and the claimant.
“There is no evidence before this court that the claimant was unwilling to cooperate with the company in this regard,” he added.
Chen’s employment was terminated on July 24, 2023, after 26 years of continuous service and without any disciplinary record.

The court awarded him back wages based on his last-drawn salary of RM9,880 per month for 22 months, plus compensation in lieu of reinstatement calculated at one month’s wage for each year of service, totalling RM474,240.
V Varunnath and Tan Jing Yi appeared for the claimant while Adrienne Sena was counsel for Astro.
407e19679fa65b8d: KUALA TERENGGANU: At a 0.4ha sanctuary in Bukit Kor, researchers are building what they believe is the largest collection of stingless bee species in the Indo-Malaya region.
Universiti Malaysia Terengganu's (UMT) Indo-Malaya Stingless Bee Repository in Marang is now home to 20 species of kelulut, including several not previously recorded in peninsular Malaysia.

Far from being simply a collection of beehives, the sanctuary is developing into a biodiversity conservation centre, complete with flowering gardens, rare heritage plants and even an enormous water lily from the Amazon.
Its founder, Shamsul Bahri Abd Razak, told Bernama the repository could play an important role in documenting and preserving the region's lesser-known pollinators.

"We believe the UMT repository houses the largest collection of stingless bee species in the Indo-Malaya region. This is an important achievement for research, conservation and biodiversity education," he said.

Among its rarer inhabitants are "Heterotrigona erythrogastra", "Tetrigona peninsularis" and "Sundatrigona moorei". Their identities have been verified through scientific inventory and taxonomic identification, making the collection a valuable reference for researchers.

Visitors can also observe differences in the bees' physical characteristics, nesting structures and behaviour, revealing a diversity that goes well beyond their familiar association with honey production.

The repository's ambitions extend beyond conserving the bees: a developing flower garden will provide nectar and pollen throughout the year, sustaining the colonies while attracting other pollinating insects.
"We are planting a variety of flowering plants with different blooming periods to ensure a steady food supply throughout the year," Shamsul highlighted.
The importance of this is reinforced by recent overseas research suggesting that some of the most valuable flowers for pollinators are those gardeners often dismiss as weeds.
A survey conducted through Britain's Pollinator Monitoring Scheme found that common ivy attracted an average of 22 flying-insect visits during each 10-minute observation, followed by hogweed with 20.
Bramble, thistles and other overlooked plants also proved popular, highlighting how diverse vegetation can support insects that depend on reliable food sources.

Although the findings concern British plants and pollinators, they illustrate a broader ecological principle relevant to UMT's efforts: sustaining insect diversity depends on maintaining plants that provide food across the seasons.
Once completed, the flower garden is also expected to become an attraction for visitors interested in biodiversity and nature-based tourism.

The sanctuary's conservation work also includes the reintroduction of four species of Kor palms. These distinctive forest plants once formed part of Bukit Kor's natural landscape, but disappeared locally after generations of agricultural land clearing.
Although only "Johannesteijsmannia altifrons" was originally distributed in Terengganu, the repository has introduced three additional species to enrich its botanical collection.

The team has further planted 400 trees representing 90 rare species, including traditional fruit trees and food plants associated with village life, while collecting forest orchids to expand the available floral resources.

Perhaps its most visually spectacular attraction is "Victoria amazonica", the giant Amazonian water lily whose circular leaves can reach 3m across under favourable conditions. Its flowers undergo an equally striking transformation, changing from white to pink over two nights.
Together, these initiatives reflect UMT's ambition to establish Bukit Kor as a distinctive centre for biodiversity education and ecotourism.

And while the giant water lilies may command the most attention, the sanctuary's smallest residents remain central to its mission, demonstrating how protecting biodiversity begins with understanding the relationships between plants and the insects that depend on them.

Beliau turut menyatakan saksi berkenaan membuat kenyataan bercanggah dengan keterangannya sendiri apabila membuat spekulasi mengenai pelbagai cara penstriman haram mungkin berlaku — termasuk cadangan isteri atau anak lelaki Chen mungkin melakukannya, sekiranya Chen berkongsi kata laluan sekali guna (OTP) telefon bimbit.

“Selain kesimpulan sambil lewa dan andaian tidak berasas dibuat oleh syarikat, pihak syarikat juga tidak mengambil langkah lebih lanjut memeriksa atau menjalankan siasatan forensik ke atas semua peranti milik penuntut atau keluarganya bagi membuktikan sebarang kaitan antara penstriman haram berkenaan dengan pihak yang menuntut.

e90c2ef2c29add89: MILAN: Zinedine Zidane was unimpressed with his side's defensive display after suffering his first defeat as France head coach against Italy on Thursday, but described the setback as "part of the process".

Les Bleus took an early lead at San Siro through Michael Olise to put one foot in the Uefa Nations League quarter-finals but were pegged back by a Francesco Pio Esposito double and Davide Frattesi strike.
Italy seized control of the game in the second half after the two sides went in level at the break following an opening period dominated by Zidane's side.

Frattesi's goal arrived three minutes after Sebastiano Esposito had missed a penalty, and France conceded a second spot kick, converted by the younger Esposito brother, to take the game beyond the visitors.
"We started well, and we were good in possession, but in the second half we ran into difficulties, especially defensively," Zidane told a press conference.

Asked if the team lacked courage, he replied, "No, quite the opposite. We stayed in the game, we did well in possession, especially in the first half, but in the second half we caved in a bit, especially after 2-1. It's part of the process."
France were twice denied by the woodwork and had 60 per cent possession and 18 attempts during an entertaining game as they slipped behind Italy into second place on head-to-head record in Group A1.
Zidane's side host Turkey, who have failed to pick up a single point thus far, in their final game on Sunday, while Italy travel to Belgium, who are one point behind in third.
"The most important thing is creating chances," Zidane added.
"Hitting the post had an impact, but I'm not disappointed. I would have been if we hadn't created good possession. What we need to analyse is why we weren't at the right level off the ball."
Mancini tips Esposito for record

France were without star attackers Kylian Mbappe and Ousmane Dembele for the trip to Milan, but Zidane denied that their absence impacted the performance and revealed that Real Madrid striker Mbappe could return against Turkey.
"I think all the players were focused. As I said, we were a little less focused and less effective in the second half," Zidane said.
"I hope (Mbappe) can play against Turkey. That is the plan, we decided not to risk him tonight because he had a little problem."
Italy coach Roberto Mancini's impressive start to his second spell continued as his side moved top and stretched their unbeaten run to four games.

Esposito's double caught the attention as the Inter Milan striker took his international tally to nine goals in 14 games, and Mancini believes he could even eye the long-standing national record held by 1968 European champion Gigi Riva.
"Let's hope he scores a lot more goals," Mancini said.
"Gigi Riva has been up there on 35 for a lifetime. Let's hope someone surpasses him. We need goals from Pio and the others too, but he can score a lot."
Esposito could have had a hat-trick had his older brother not taken – and missed – Italy's first penalty of the match during the second half, a moment Mancini revealed was not part of the plan.
"Pio is first choice, and then Sebastiano. It was a family thing," Mancini laughed.

c25e0ee06ffb0b6f: PETALING JAYA: Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) dan Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) berpotensi memperkukuh sokongan pengundi B40 terhadap Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim dan Pakatan Harapan (PH), kata penganalisis.
Bagaimanapun, mereka berkata bantuan itu tidak semestinya menjamin sokongan politik berkekalan kerana pengundi turut menilai keberkesanan kerajaan menangani tekanan kos sara hidup.
Azmi Hassan dari Akademi Nusantara berkata kedua-dua program itu berpeluang menjadi legasi Anwar, seperti Bantuan Rakyat 1Malaysia (BR1M) yang sinonim dengan bekas perdana menteri Najib Razak.
Menurutnya, STR meneruskan pendekatan bantuan tunai seperti BR1M, manakala SARA memperluas manfaat kepada penerima melalui pembelian barangan keperluan asas menggunakan MyKad.
Beliau berkata walaupun jumlah bantuan itu mungkin dianggap kecil bagi sesetengah pihak, golongan B40 amat menghargainya kerana dapat membantu meringankan beban kewangan secara berkala.
"Jadi, ia dapat bantu Anwar raih undi," katanya kepada FMT.
STR disalurkan secara berperingkat kepada penerima layak, manakala SARA menyediakan kredit melalui MyKad untuk pembelian barangan keperluan asas.
Pada 2026, isi rumah yang memenuhi syarat tertentu layak menerima gabungan STR dan SARA sehingga RM4,600 setahun, merangkumi STR maksimum RM2,200 dan SARA sehingga RM2,400.

Kerajaan memperuntukkan RM15 bilion bagi kedua-dua program itu tahun ini, berbanding RM6.8 bilion untuk BR1M pada 2017. Peruntukan STR dan SARA turut ditingkatkan kepada RM16 bilion dalam Belanjawan 2027.

Awang Azman Pawi dari Universiti Malaya pula berkata kekuatan BR1M terletak pada kesannya terhadap kehidupan rakyat sehingga membentuk persepsi bahawa pentadbiran Najib mengambil langkah membantu golongan berdepan tekanan kewangan.
Menurutnya, Najib mempunyai kelebihan kerana memperkenalkan BR1M pada 2012, manakala Anwar berpeluang membina legasi menerusi peluasan dan penambahbaikan sistem bantuan sedia ada.
Bagaimanapun, beliau mengingatkan peruntukan lebih besar tidak semestinya menghasilkan sokongan politik lebih kukuh kerana pengundi turut menilai keberkesanan bantuan dalam menangani kos sara hidup.
Beliau mengambil contoh BR1M yang memberi manfaat kepada sebahagian penerima, namun tidak mampu menghalang kekalahan Barisan Nasional (BN) ketika PRU14 pada 2018.

"Sokongan politik tidak berlaku secara automatik. Pengundi juga menilai sama ada pendapatan mereka mencukupi, harga makanan mampu ditanggung, peluang pekerjaan semakin baik dan taraf kehidupan keluarga menunjukkan peningkatan," katanya.

Awang Azman berkata STR dan SARA mampu memperkukuh keyakinan terhadap pentadbiran Anwar, tetapi sokongan lebih berkekalan bergantung kepada peningkatan pendapatan sebenar, kestabilan harga barangan dan peluang rakyat memperbaiki taraf hidup.
"Pada akhirnya, sebesar mana pun bantuan kerajaan, keyakinan rakyat bergantung pada satu persoalan utama, iaitu adakah kehidupan mereka benar-benar menjadi lebih baik?" katanya.
Bantuan ringankan beban penerima di Melaka
Di Melaka, beberapa penerima STR dan SARA yang ditemui FMT mengakui bantuan itu membantu meringankan perbelanjaan harian, khususnya untuk keperluan keluarga.

Faizal Saadon, 40, berkata SARA membantunya membeli barangan dapur, manakala STR berjumlah RM1,800 yang diterima sepanjang tahun ini digunakan untuk pelbagai perbelanjaan keluarga, termasuk persekolahan anak-anak.

Pengundi di DUN Bemban yang bekerja sebagai pekerja am di sebuah syarikat penghantaran itu turut menggunakan sebahagian bantuan STR diterima pada fasa kedua, bersama wang gajinya, untuk memperbaharui cukai jalan kenderaan yang tamat tempoh.
"Ia meringankan beban saya," katanya.

Bagi Shamsuri Mohd Salleh, 57, peniaga di DUN Rim, bantuan STR dan SARA bukan sahaja meringankan perbelanjaan keluarga, malah membantu menampung kos pembelian bahan mentah untuk perniagaan makanannya.
Menurutnya, bantuan STR juga berguna ketika musim perayaan kerana dapat digunakan untuk membeli barangan keperluan sambutan.
"STR membantu. (Pada hari) perayaan saya dapat juga duit. Jadi dapatlah membantu membeli barang-barang (perayaan)," katanya.
Sementara itu, Ria Artika Nor, 38, peniaga dan pengundi DUN Merlimau, berkata bantuan berkenaan membolehkannya membeli barangan dapur serta memenuhi keperluan anak-anak.
Bagaimanapun, beliau berharap jumlah bantuan STR sebanyak RM1,200 setahun dan SARA RM100 sebulan yang diterimanya dapat ditingkatkan bagi meringankan beban keluarga susulan kenaikan harga barangan.
a106566e6948edaf: WASHINGTON: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is closely monitoring volatility in AI equity valuations and the US political shift that could slow data center development, but says it is too early to tell whether investors are souring on the sector for the long term.

IMF spokesperson Julie Kozack told a regular press briefing that AI equity valuations remain exposed to a reassessment of the longer-term profitability of the technology. "That overall view that we have taken still remains the case," she said.

The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang sent the company's shares sharply lower on Thursday, dragging down the S&P 500 and Nasdaq indexes, but some major tech stocks rose, including Nvidia rival Advanced Micro Devices, Alphabet and Microsoft.

Asked about the impact on the AI sector from the stock gyrations, as well as pledges by newly elected Democratic governors to slow data center development, Kozack said: "We're of course are closely monitoring the most recent developments and their impact on equity markets, the economy, and financial stability, but at this point it's really too early to say whether there's going to be some broader reassessment of investment in AI technology and any broader reassessment of profitability and future productivity gains."
Kozack also said it was too early to determine any impact on US inflation pressures from possible shifts in AI investment "just based on what we've seen in the past hours, weeks, and days."

She said the IMF views the increased demand created by AI investment and data center construction as one of the two major contributors to US inflation, along with elevated energy prices caused by the Iran war and closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
The IMF believes that the Federal Reserve will still need to maintain restrictive US monetary policy to bring inflation back to its 2% target, Kozack said.

"Our view is that a restrictive policy stance will be necessary going forward to support disinflation and bring inflation gradually back to target. We fully support the Fed's focus on price stability and its readiness to act as needed to bring inflation down," Kozack said.
The Fed's policy-setting committee next meets on Dec 8-9.

7f11750ed4bd7938: Five minutes into a pitch from a former English teacher in 2000, a Japanese tycoon decided he had seen enough and handed him over about US$20 million, roughly RM81 million at today's rates. The tycoon was Masayoshi Son, the teacher was Jack Ma, and by the time Alibaba listed in 2014, CNBC reckoned Son's stake was worth US$50 billion (RM203 billion) or more.
Son's explanation was pure instinct: "It was the look in his eye, it was an 'animal smell'."
That same RM203 billion is what Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim says Son now wants to spend here in Malaysia. Let that sink in for a bit.

Speaking in Melaka on Oct 24, Anwar said the SoftBank Group founder had told him over a video call days earlier that he had picked Kuching in Sarawak and sites in Peninsular Malaysia for some US$50 billion of investment. "In what areas? AI, new technology and data centres," Anwar said.
A man who bets big, and sometimes loses big

Son is no stranger to numbers like these. At the height of the dot-com bubble he was, for three days, the richest man on earth, before SoftBank's shares fell 93% by the end of 2000 and, by Bloomberg's tally, some US$70 billion (RM284 billion) of his fortune went up in smoke.

SoftBank later poured billions into WeWork, the office-sharing firm once valued at a whopping US$47 billion (RM191 billion), only to watch it file for bankruptcy in 2023. Yet Son bounced back again, and in June Forbes crowned him Asia's richest person, with US$97 billion (RM394 billion) to his name.
Why Malaysia, and why now?

The answer lies in Son's obsession with artificial superintelligence (ASI), AI that vastly outperforms the brightest humans, which he predicted in 2024 would be 10,000 times smarter than us within a decade. "I think I was born to realise ASI. I am super serious about it," he told shareholders that June.

Superintelligence needs gargantuan amounts of computing power, and computing power needs land, electricity and water. That's why SoftBank has already sunk about US$64.6 billion (RM262 billion) into OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, and is planning a US$500 billion (RM2 trillion) data centre campus in Ohio.

Here in Malaysia, he finds what few other countries can offer: RM385.7 billion of data centre-related investment recorded since 2021, according to the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA), a government pitching us as neutral, non-aligned ground for technology and, in Sarawak, a state energy company ready to supply the power.

On Oct 8, Son signed a framework agreement with Petroleum Sarawak (Petros) and Grab to explore an AI and digital infrastructure platform in Sarawak. Talk about coming full circle: Grab began life as MyTeksi in Kuala Lumpur in 2012, and SoftBank backed it with US$250 million (RM1 billion) in 2014.
What's in it for you?

The sum is about a tenth of our economy, which the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) put at RM2.03 trillion last year, and more than three times the RM61 billion that Google pledged here on Nov 4.

But here's the thing: data centres are heavy on capital and light on people. The 27 projects approved by the government's Data Centre Task Force, worth RM225.97 billion, are expected to create just 4,053 jobs, or more than RM55 million of investment per job.

Sure, 3,523 of those are high-skilled roles in engineering, networking and cybersecurity, and Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo told Parliament on Oct 28 that Malaysians were expected to fill nearly 90% of them.

I can't help but feel the bigger prize is everything around the servers. Google expects its expansion to support more than 37,000 construction jobs a year but more than 9,000 once the campuses run, and the Sarawak pact lists robotics and local workforce development.
So how do we make sure Malaysians collect on Son's bet? Three things.
1. Get it in writing

SoftBank's only public word so far, an emailed statement reported by Dow Jones, says it is exploring AI and digital infrastructure opportunities with the government and others, but confirms no figure. Nikkei Asia reports it would fund only part of it, with financiers and partners covering the rest.
Putrajaya and Sarawak should publish a phased schedule with dated milestones and SoftBank's own share, so the public can tell a pledge from a project.
2. Make the jobs and contracts Malaysian
The Data Centre Task Force already requires at least 30% local content from approved projects.

For a deal this size, that floor should rise, and SoftBank, which brings robotics and "physical AI" to the Sarawak pact, should train Malaysian technicians there, with MIDA publishing what was being spent locally each year.
3. Make the servers pay for their own power
Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Johari Ghani has said data centres on Tenaga Nasional Berhad's (TNB) grid pay market rates without subsidies, and pay for every megawatt they reserve.

Son should go one step further, as Google did when it pledged to add over 1GW of clean energy to the grid without public subsidies, so that no household in Kuching or Klang pays a sen more for his servers.

Son once turned RM81 million and an "animal smell" into a stake worth upwards of RM203 billion. He is now offering Malaysia a bet of the same size, and it's up to Putrajaya to make sure that this time, ordinary Malaysians hold a share of the winnings.

b79e0301be83fbd1: PETALING JAYA: Imagine sitting down to eat a meal and hearing three different opinions before you take your first bite.
“Better stop eating rice.”
“That papaya is too sweet for you.”
“Use honey instead of sugar. It’s healthier.”
For many Malaysians living with diabetes, familiar meals can suddenly feel like a test. Advice comes from relatives, friends and social media, often with good intentions but little explanation.
Food choices become easier when you understand the reasoning behind the advice. Here are five common diabetes food myths worth reconsidering:
Myth 1: I must stop eating rice
For someone who has eaten rice all their life, being told to give it up can make diabetes feel especially daunting.
Rice contains starch, which your body breaks down into glucose. But so do noodles, bread and potatoes. Swapping rice for a large plate of mee hoon does not automatically mean less carbohydrate.

The portion and the rest of your meal matter. The next time you’re tucking into “nasi campur”, follow the health ministry’s “Suku-Suku Separuh” portion guide by filling half your plate with non-starchy vegetables, one-quarter with a lean protein such as fish, chicken, tofu or eggs, and one-quarter with rice.
This is a starting point, with portions adjusted to your needs. Rice can remain part of the meal without taking up most of the plate.
Myth 2: Sweet fruit is forbidden
Picture a family sharing freshly cut papaya. Someone with diabetes declines, worried that anything tasting sweet must be unsuitable.
Yet whole fruit supplies fibre, vitamins and minerals alongside its natural sugars. Sweetness alone cannot indicate how much carbohydrate a serving contains.
Mangoes, bananas and papaya can fit into a diabetes eating plan. The practical question is how much you eat. Ask, “What is a suitable portion for me?” rather than banning the fruit altogether.
Serve a small portion rather than eating directly from a large shared platter. Use a small Chinese rice bowl or a tea cup as a portion guide for a serving of cut fruit.
Myth 3: Honey and gula Melaka are safer because they are natural
A spoonful of honey in warm water can feel more wholesome than sugar stirred into tea. But your body still receives sugar from it.
Honey, gula Melaka and any type of sugar contribute carbohydrates and can raise blood glucose. Their natural origins do not make them unlimited choices.
Rather than searching for a “safe” sugar, gradually reduce how sweet your drinks taste. Order unsweetened tea or “kopi O kosong”, and remember that “kurang manis” still means some sweetness remains.
The useful question is, “How much am I adding?”
Myth 4: Foods labelled ‘sugar-free’ are always better for diabetes

While shopping in your supermarket, you spot sugar-free biscuits and assume they must be a better choice for managing your blood glucose. The label sounds reassuring, but it tells only part of the story.
Sugar-free biscuits can still contain flour, which provides carbohydrate that breaks down into glucose. They may also contain as much fat and calories as regular biscuits.

Look beyond the claim on the front. Compare the carbohydrate content and serving size on the nutrition label. If the information is for two biscuits but you eat six, you are having three times the amount listed.
Choose foods for their overall nutritional value and the portion you eat, rather than relying on “sugar-free” labels.
Myth 5: I can never enjoy dessert again
At a family gathering, avoiding every favourite cake or kuih may feel isolating. Diabetes does not necessarily require a lifelong ban on dessert.
Portion, frequency and your overall meal intake matter. Choose one small piece of the kuih you most enjoy, rather than sampling several, and pair it with unsweetened tea instead of teh tarik.
Your dietitian can help you work occasional treats into your balanced eating plan.
Whenever food advice sounds absolute, take a pause and think about it. It may just be a belief that has turned into a long-standing myth.
Healthy eating with diabetes should give you understanding and confidence, while leaving room for the Malaysian foods and shared meals you love.

Indra Balaratnam is a consultant dietitian and a fellow of the Malaysian Dietitians’ Association. She runs her own private practice, Indra Balaratnam Nutrition, in Kuala Lumpur. Connect with her on Facebook and Instagram.

f943ad13d534492f: The US government on Thursday said it had obtained court authorization to seize or restrain use of over $1.2 billion stolen during last month's $6.3 billion Binance heist, as part of a larger effort to disrupt North Korea's ongoing cryptocurrency theft.

The court also allowed the takedown of cloud-based infrastructure used in a Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) social engineering scheme called “FaceStealer” that has amassed more than $400 million in the last 18 months.

It’s called FaceStealer because it involved secretly recorded webcam videos. Victims are typically people working in the cryptocurrency and web3 industries, along with open source software developers and maintainers who DPRK hackers target in the hope of accessing the software repositories they control as the first step towards creating supply chain attacks.
900+ faces stolen
The FBI said it had seized more than 900 webcam videos belonging to these tech workers.
Here’s how the attack works.
First, the North Koreans send targets an invitation to join a video meeting. Those invitations come from hijacked accounts that the next intended victim may find familiar or credible.

“You're going to think it's real because it's going to be based on either conversations or interests you've expressed in the past with this actual person,” said special agent Jeremy Robertson, who oversees counterintelligence and cyber investigations at FBI Los Angeles.
“They're going to then send you a link to catch up, and it's usually a calendar invite, and it's going to have some typo-squatted URLs in there,” he told reporters on Thursday.

The URL directs the victim to a fake Zoom or Teams meeting, and the cybercriminals record the target’s webcam video while playing a phony, prerecorded video of the person who purportedly sent the meeting invite.
Sometimes the hackers also use deepfake videos of well-known individuals in the cryptocurrency and web3 industries, we’re told.

“When you log in, whoever invited you – your friend or business associate – is going to be on the screen, but you're not going to hear any audio,” Robertson said. “But you're going to see their face, you're going to see them looking around, you're going to see them mouthing some words, and then in the text box you're going to receive some instructions.”
‘You’re on mute’ as a social engineering vector

The text box tells the victim that the person on the other end of the video call can’t hear them, they need to upgrade their software for the audio to work properly, and it sends a link to the supposed fix.
Clicking to access the “fix” installs cryptocurrency-stealing malware on the victim’s computer and sends their contact list to the digital thieves to perpetuate the scam.

The FBI attributes FaceStealer to a North Korea-linked group tracked as Sapphire Sleet, which is widely regarded as a Lazarus Group offshoot. Sapphire Sleet is also known as UNC1069, Stardust Chollima, APT38, and BlueNoroff.

“The actors behind this activity, commonly referred to as Sapphire Sleet and other associated names, are part of a broader North Korean effort to generate revenue for the regime, to steal virtual assets, and gain access to networks and trusted online ecosystems,” Brett Leatherman, assistant director of the FBI's Cyber Division, told reporters. “North Korean hackers are increasingly blending cyber intrusion, social engineering, and emerging technologies such as deep fakes to make their impersonation efforts more convincing and scalable.”
Binance heist update

The FBI also provided an update on its efforts to recover the stolen assets from the October 29 attack on Binance. The agency previously blamed the $6.3 billion heist on TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking operation also linked to Lazarus Group.

Last week, Binance revealed the attackers laid the groundwork for their “sophisticated, multi-stage campaign” back in June, and said it involved social engineering during fake job interviews, malware downloads, compromised internal AI tooling, endpoint takeover, and an “advanced transaction-authorization method.”

Since the theft, federal investigators and private-sector partners have helped freeze more than $2.7 billion in stolen assets. The Justice Department's court authorization covers more than $1.2 billion of that haul.®
48c952fbb3812d58: WASHINGTON: The US government started the 2027 fiscal year with a US$404 billion budget deficit for October, a record for the month and US$120 billion, or 42%, higher than the year-earlier period, as receipts shrank and outlays grew sharply, the Treasury Department said on Thursday.

October receipts fell by US$35 billion, or 9%, to US$369 billion, due partly to lower net customs duty collections. Individual non-withheld taxes were US$29 billion, or 36%, lower than year-ago levels, which were swelled by tax filing deadlines delayed for Californians affected by the 2025 wildfires.

After calendar-related adjustments made because benefit payments for November were shifted into October for both fiscal years, the Treasury said the adjusted deficit would have been US$285 billion, an increase of US$94 billion, or 49%, from the year-ago period.

But the reported October outlays came to a record for that month of US$773 billion, up US$84 billion, or 12%, from year-ago levels. The outlay increases were driven in part by a US$14 billion, or 80%, increase in US Department of Agriculture spending due to farm relief payments and a US$28 billion, or 30%, increase in military spending, representing an October payment to military trust funds that was delayed by last year's government shutdown, along with increases spread across operations, maintenance and procurement.
Gross interest on the federal debt also rose US$11 billion, or 11%, from the previous October to US$115 billion.

10fd078bb6738e75: PETALING JAYA: Two cash aid initiatives – Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) – may boost support among B40 voters for Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and Pakatan Harapan (PH), analysts say.

Azmi Hassan of Akademi Nusantara said the two programmes could become part of Anwar's political legacy, much like Bantuan Rakyat 1Malaysia (BR1M), which remains closely associated with former prime minister Najib Razak.
He said STR continued BR1M's cash assistance approach, while SARA expanded the benefits by allowing recipients to purchase essential goods using their MyKad.
Azmi said although some might consider the amount of assistance to be relatively small, the B40 group greatly appreciated the regular financial relief.
"So, it could help Anwar win votes," he told FMT ahead of the Melaka polls on Saturday.
PH, which Anwar chairs, will be contesting 21 seats in the state election.
STR provides cash assistance in phases to eligible recipients, while SARA offers credits through MyKad for purchasing essential goods.

Awang Azman Pawi of Universiti Malaya said BR1M's strength lay in its impact on people's lives, shaping the perception that Najib's administration had taken steps to help those facing financial difficulties.
He said Najib had the advantage of introducing BR1M in 2012, while Anwar had an opportunity to build his own legacy by expanding and improving the existing assistance system.

However, Awang Azman cautioned that larger allocations did not necessarily translate into stronger political support, as voters also assessed how effectively the assistance helped them cope with living costs.
He cited BR1M as an example of a programme that benefited some recipients but failed to prevent Barisan Nasional's defeat in the 2018 general election.

"Political support does not come automatically. Voters also assess whether their income is sufficient, food prices are affordable, job opportunities are improving and their families' standard of living is getting better.”

Awang Azman said STR and SARA could strengthen confidence in Anwar's administration, but lasting support would depend on improvements in real incomes, price stability and opportunities for people to improve their living standards.
"Ultimately, regardless of how much assistance the government provides, public confidence comes down to one fundamental question – are people's lives genuinely getting better?”
Financial aid eases burden for Melaka recipients
In Melaka, several STR and SARA recipients interviewed by FMT acknowledged that the assistance helped ease their daily expenses.

Faizal Saadon, 40, said SARA helped him purchase groceries, while the RM1,800 in STR assistance he received this year went towards various household expenses, including his children's schooling needs.
The Bemban voter, who works for a delivery company, also used part of his STR payment, together with his salary, to renew his expired road tax.
"It eases my burden,” he said.

For Shamsuri Salleh, 57, a food stall operator in the Rim constituency, STR and SARA not only helped ease his family's household expenses but also covered the cost of raw ingredients for his food business.
He said STR was also useful during festive seasons, as the money could be spent on items needed for the celebrations.
"STR helps. During festive celebrations, I also receive money. So it helps me buy things (for the celebrations).”
Meanwhile, entrepreneur Ria Artika Nor, 38, said the money enabled her to purchase groceries and provide for her children's needs.

However, Ria, who is from Merlimau, hopes the RM1,200 in annual STR assistance and RM100 in monthly SARA credits she currently receives could be increased to help ease her family's financial burden amid rising prices.
